issues.issue: Source Eq. (5) displays an unsquared norm, whereas the smoothness prose and p.4 proof use quadratic smoothness. This reference assessment is expressly limited to the quadratic inequality in the first assumption. Literal Eq. (5) is not asserted equivalent, and no author correction is established.

evidence.statement_check: Theorem 1 and its required algorithm, assumptions and proof visually checked on PDF pp.2-5. The explicit quadratic smoothness interpretation supports a restricted source-linked reference assessment; the source interpretation remains explicit.

content.intended_use: Bound expected objective error of the selected SVRG Option II algorithm under the explicit quadratic smoothness interpretation.

proofs.locator: PDF p.4 proof following Figure 1, Eq. (8), and p.5 first three proof displays through QED
map: p.4: define g_i(w)=psi_i(w)-psi_i(w*)-<grad psi_i(w*),w-w*>. Convexity gives minimum zero at w*. Quadratic smoothness and a descent step give ||grad psi_i(w)-grad psi_i(w*)||^2 <= 2L g_i(w).
p.4 Eq. (8): average the component inequality and use grad P(w*)=0 to obtain n^{-1} sum_i ||grad psi_i(w)-grad psi_i(w*)||^2 <= 2L(P(w)-P*).

p.4: express v_t using current and centered snapshot gradient differences. Apply ||a+b||^2 <= 2||a||^2+2||b||^2 and E||X-EX||^2 <= E||X||^2, then Eq. (8), giving E||v_t||^2 <= 4L(gap_current+gap_snapshot).
p.4 last display: conditional unbiasedness E v_t=grad P(w_{t-1}) and convexity imply E||w_t-w*||^2 <= ||w_{t-1}-w*||^2-2eta(1-2Leta)(P(w_{t-1})-P*)+4Leta^2(P(wtilde)-P*).

p.5 first display: sum t=1,...,m and take all-history expectation. Option II turns the average of gaps for w_0,...,w_{m-1} into the expected next snapshot gap. Bound initial squared distance by 2(P(wtilde)-P*)/gamma using Eq. (6).
p.5 next displays: drop the nonnegative final squared distance and divide by 2eta(1-2Leta)m to obtain epoch factor alpha; iterate over epochs.
proofs.omitted_details: Faithful source proof map; algebra is not reproduced as an independent complete local proof. No local transfer or author correction is claimed. proofs.reading_coverage: Actually viewed p.4 Figure 1 and proof through distance recursion, and p.5 proof completion; checked p.3 statement and p.2 standing displays.

assumptions: Each component is convex and smooth. Require explicitly psi_i(x) <= psi_i(y)+<grad psi_i(y),x-y>+(L/2)||x-y||_2^2 for every i,x,y. This quadratic smoothness condition is an interpretation of the source prose and proof: displayed Eq. (5) on p.2 visibly lacks the square. This record assesses Theorem 1 only under the explicit quadratic condition, without asserting equivalence to the literal display or an author correction.
P(x) >= P(y)+<grad P(y),x-y>+(gamma/2)||x-y||_2^2 for all x,y, as in Eq. (6), with gamma>0.
Use Figure 1 Option II with exact snapshot full gradient and paired component gradients, fresh uniform component indices, and an independent uniform output index J in {0,...,m-1}.
statement.conclusion: E[P(wtilde_s)-P*] <= alpha^s Delta_0. This is the source-linked contraction under the explicit quadratic smoothness interpretation stated above; it makes no claim based solely on the literal unsquared Eq. (5).
statement.objects_and_definitions: For positive integers n,d, let differentiable convex psi_i:R^d -> R and P=n^{-1} sum_i psi_i. Let w* minimize P, P*=P(w*), and Delta_0=P(wtilde_0)-P* for a fixed initial point. All norms are Euclidean. Define alpha=1/[gamma*eta*(1-2L*eta)*m]+2L*eta/(1-2L*eta).
statement.parameter_domains: n,d,m positive integers; 0<gamma<=L; eta>0 with 1-2L*eta>0 and alpha<1. These explicit positive-denominator domains state the regime used in the proof; the displayed theorem itself says m is sufficiently large so alpha<1.
statement.quantifiers_and_randomness: For every such finite sum, fixed initial point and admissible tuning, and every integer s>=0, expectation is over all component draws and epoch output selections through epoch s.
